core_claim.P: injectAndCall is called directly on the router contract rather than in a delegatecall context
core_claim.I: injectAndCall must be restricted to delegatecall-only execution (onlyDelegatecall) so it operates on the caller's wallet balances, not the router's storage/balance
core_claim.V: injectAndCall lacks an onlyDelegatecall restriction, so anyone can call it directly on the router, causing _getSelfBalance(token) to read the router's balance and allowing arbitrary target calls with injected router balances

distinct_impacts.description: Attackers can invoke injectAndCall directly and potentially drain ETH or ERC20 tokens from the router
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Attackers can invoke `injectAndCall` directly and potentially drain ETH or ERC20 tokens from the router.

distinct_impacts.description: User wallet balances remain untouched, breaking the expected wallet isolation behavior
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: User wallet balances remain untouched, breaking the expected behavior.

distinct_impacts.description: _getSelfBalance(token) reads the router's balance instead of the intended user wallet's balance when called directly
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: The contract itself becomes the caller, so `_getSelfBalance(token)` reads the router’s balance instead of the intended user wallet’s balance.

distinct_impacts.description: Arbitrary target calls may be executed with injected balances from the router instead of the wallet
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Arbitrary target calls may be executed with injected balances from the router instead of the wallet.
